symptoms.question: When you try to start the car, does the engine crank or turn over? (yes/no)
When the ignition is on, are the dashboard lights bright and normal? (yes/no)
Is the battery/charging system warning light on while driving? (yes/no)
Is the check engine warning light on while driving? (yes/no)
Does the check engine light flash while driving (not just stay on)? (yes/no)
Does the engine sometimes stall or cut out while idling? (yes/no)
Does the engine run rough or uneven when idling? (yes/no)
Is the car especially hard to start when the engine is cold? (yes/no)
Do you sometimes smell fuel around the engine bay? (yes/no)

rules.diagnosis: Engine does not crank and dashboard lights are dim, suggesting a weak battery or bad battery connection.
rules.advice: Do not keep trying to start repeatedly. Check battery terminals if safe, and consider calling roadside assistance or jump-starting.

rules.diagnosis: Engine does not crank but dashboard lights are normal, suggesting a starter motor or ignition circuit issue.
rules.advice: Avoid repeated start attempts. Have the starting system inspected by a mechanic.

rules.diagnosis: Battery/charging warning light indicates a possible alternator or charging system fault.
rules.advice: Turn off non-essential electrical loads and drive only to a safe place or a garage. The car may stop once the battery is depleted.

rules.diagnosis: The check engine light indicates an engine management fault that may affect emissions or performance.
rules.advice: Drive gently and have fault codes read soon. If the light flashes or the engine misfires badly, stop driving.

rules.diagnosis: A flashing check engine light often indicates severe misfire or a problem that can damage the catalytic converter.
rules.advice: Reduce load immediately. If the engine runs very rough, stop driving and seek professional help.

rules.diagnosis: Stalling at idle can be caused by air intake, idle control, fuel or ignition issues.
rules.advice: Avoid situations where stalling is dangerous (e.g., intersections). Have the car inspected and fault codes read.

rules.diagnosis: Rough idle often suggests misfire, air intake leaks, fuel mixture issues, or ignition problems.
rules.advice: Have ignition and intake checked and fault codes read if the check engine light is on.
